evidence.observation: The first viewport names Jamie, the target role family, the value proposition, and direct paths to work, resume, and contact.
The page maps delivery coordination, risk surfacing, documentation, launch support, and handoffs to named projects and specific proof points.
The business result remains contribution language, while private dashboards, customer data, and unsupported causal ownership remain outside the claim.
Jamie's attributed planning and presenter roles are separated from Board and Council decisions, and appropriation is explicitly distinguished from receipt, expenditure, or completion.
Event chronology, Council attribution, Jamie's independent follow-on, press coverage, and archived status resolve to local references with accessible backlinks and bounded support.

The citation system exposes source-specific support for founding affiliation, organizing, testimony, campaign interfaces, press records, and legislative outcomes without assigning collective results to Jamie alone.
Clear headings and direct contribution language keep the long case study usable, but repeated boundary explanations and the stacked evidence sections add scanning cost.
Jamie is plainly the builder of the independent prototype, the resident-facing result is understandable in one pass, and the page rejects official-service or hackathon-winner inflation.

The page states the Council appropriation directly while preserving the distinction between Jamie's contribution, municipal decisions, and unproven downstream funding stages; source-attributed framing keeps it just short of exceptional editorial ease.

Experimental media, prototypes, installations, gatherings, participation, memory, and place are explicitly connected to Jamie's current systems practice, though the application offers few material or visual specimens.
The case shows a clear movement from civic records to an issue model, interface, and social pathway, while the broader recursive method remains more often stated than demonstrated visually.
The artifact gallery describes a prototype, translation layer, and press record through text-only cards; no approved project image or inspectable visual artifact is rendered.
The public role title, operating-structure proposition, selected impact, and CallNYC chronology align with the homepage and the passing deterministic resume gate.

Candidate-bound evidence reports visible focus for all 24 traversed controls, including citations, and no overflow across all declared mobile and reflow checks; the zoom test used an equivalent viewport rather than browser chrome.
Canonical, Open Graph, Twitter-card, download, and contact paths are present and coherent, but the inspected candidate still uses staging metadata defaults.

Local route, accessibility, metadata, and resume checks support an application release, while matching production deploy SHAs, smoke evidence, indexing verification, and rollback proof remain an allowed application-profile deferral.

smallestDefensiblePatch: Replace one text-only CallNYC artifact card with one approved public-safe image of the surviving issue-pathway interface, accompanied by concise alt text and a caption stating exactly what the image proves while retaining the archived and unofficial boundary.
